validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real, well-documented pipeline. Opened all 3 citations harvested from the gem.wiki page (naturalgasintel.com article, nortexmidstream.com/facilities, prnewswire Tailwater Capital acquisition release) -- the full harvested pool for this row, none skipped. The Natural Gas Intelligence article (dated 2007-10-23, contemporaneous trade press, independent of GEM) is the anchor source: 'Falcon Gas Storage Co. Inc. subsidiary NorTex Gas Storage Co. LLC started flowing gas through its newly constructed Worsham-Steed Pipeline... a 60-mile, 24-inch high-pressure pipeline... [t]raversing Jack, Parker and Hood counties[,] the pipeline has a capacity of 450,000 Mcf/d, which can be expanded to 650,000 Mcf/d.' This confirms, by itself, every spec GEM carries: Status=operating (since 2007), StartYear1=2007, LengthKnown=60 mi, Diameter=24 in, Capacity=450,000 Mcf/d, Fuel=Gas, State/Country=Texas/United States. No material disagreement found anywhere.

CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission/takeaway line associated with the Worsham-Steed gas storage facility -- it interconnects with three named export pipelines (Energy Transfer's Old Ocean, Enterprise/Energy Transfer's North Texas Pipeline, Atmos Energy's Line X) and serves the Barnett Shale/DFW market, i.e. a real transmission asset, not a small gathering stub. Correctly a distinct GGIT gas row.

DUPLICATE: checked against the 45-row TX-operating roster. P4415 'Hill Lake Pipeline' is the sibling NorTex/Williams storage-associated pipeline but is a physically separate asset (different storage reservoir/county emphasis, 17 mi vs 60 mi) -- no overlap with P4416. The current operator page (williams.com/pipeline/nortex-storage/, formerly nortexmidstream.com/facilities, 302-redirects there now) separately lists 'Worsham-Steed Pipeline Capacity: 450,000 Mcf/d' at Hood County alongside a distinct 'Worsham-Steed Gas Storage' entry (Jack County) -- confirms the pipeline and the storage reservoir are correctly kept as separate concepts, and GEM's single pipeline row (vs. the storage facility, which is out of GGIT's scope) is the right unit of account. No double-count.

CORROBORATION beyond the anchor article: (1) the current Williams/NorTex Storage operator page independently restates 'Worsham-Steed Pipeline Capacity: 450,000 Mcf/d' and 'Location: Hood County, Texas' -- a second, independent, present-day origin (the operator's own current site, distinct from the 2007 trade-press story) that corroborates Capacity and Texas/Hood-County location. (2) The Worsham-Steed Gas Storage, LLC Statement of Operating Conditions on file with FERC (self-filed tariff, but a third distinct origin/document type from both the trade press and the marketing page) repeatedly confirms the entity operates 'Facilities in Jack, Hood, and Parker Counties, Texas' and is an active NGA Section-311-exempt intrastate operation -- corroborates Status=operating and the Texas/tri-county location, though it does not restate pipe diameter/length/capacity (it's a rate tariff, not an engineering spec sheet). Together this gives Status, Location and Capacity 2+ independent corroborating origins (tier=high); StartYear1, Length and Diameter rest on the single NGI account alone (tier=medium) -- a strong, detailed, contemporaneous source, but no second document was found stating the exact mileage/diameter/year, so flagging that as the residual caveat.

OWNERSHIP CHAIN (context only, not in this row's owed ref set -- Operator/Owner sit on the separate operators/owners tab, not touched here): Falcon Gas Storage Co. (2007, per NGI) -> NorTex Midstream Partners (per the 2021 PR Newswire release, Tailwater Capital LLC signed to acquire NorTex Midstream Partners, 2021-02-17 -- the release does not name Worsham-Steed specifically, it's a company-level acquisition announcement) -> now branded as Williams Companies' 'NorTex Storage' (the nortexmidstream.com domain 302-redirects to williams.com/pipeline/nortex-storage/, dateModified 2026-02-02, still live and describing Worsham-Steed as an active asset). This is a genuine ownership succession, not evidence of anything wrong with the row; flagging only so a future Owner/Operator sweep on the OO tab knows the entity has changed hands twice since 2007.

fills.researcher_notes: NGI (2007) documents the pipeline going into service; Williams' current NorTex Storage page (2026, formerly nortexmidstream.com/facilities, 302-redirect confirmed) still lists 'Worsham-Steed Pipeline' as an active facility with a stated capacity -- two independent origins, ~19 years apart, both consistent with continuous operating status.

Both sources describe it as a natural gas pipeline serving a natural gas storage facility (NGI: 'started flowing gas'; Williams: 'natural gas storage and transportation... Worsham-Steed Pipeline Capacity: 450,000 Mcf/d'). No indication of NGL/oil/other commodity.

NGI's article is a contemporaneous news report published 2007-10-23 (verified in the article's own schema.org datePublished field, not just its dateline) headlined 'Falcon's Worsham-Steed Pipeline Begins Flowing Gas' and stating the company 'started flowing gas through its newly constructed Worsham-Steed Pipeline... the company said Monday.' This is strong, direct, primary-source evidence for the 2007 start year, but I could not find a second independent document that separately states the exact year, so tier=medium (single strong source) rather than high.

NGI: 'a 60-mile, 24-inch high-pressure pipeline in the western portion of the Barnett Shale play in North Texas.' Matches GEM exactly (60.00 mi). Williams' current operator page gives capacity and location for the pipeline but does not restate mileage, so this rests on one source -- tier=medium. Sanity check: Williams' combined NorTex Storage system (Worsham-Steed + Hill-Lake) is described elsewhere on that page as '~80 miles of natural gas transmission pipelines' total, consistent with 60 mi (P4416) + 17 mi (P4415, Hill Lake Pipeline) = 77 mi -- no red flag.

Same NGI sentence gives '24-inch' diameter, matching GEM exactly. Single-source (tier=medium) -- no second document states pipe diameter; the FERC/RRC tariff filings and the operator's current facilities page give capacity and location but not diameter.

NGI: pipeline 'traversing Jack, Parker and Hood counties' in Texas. The Worsham-Steed Gas Storage, LLC FERC Statement of Operating Conditions (PDF; url_verifier's automated substring screen returned a content FAIL because it can only screen HTML text, not PDF bytes -- a documented false-negative pattern for PDFs -- so I downloaded it and confirmed with `pdftotext -layout` that it repeatedly states services are 'performed by Worsham-Steed through its Facilities in Jack, Hood, and Parker Counties, Texas'; URL itself verifies OK/200) independently corroborates the same three-county Texas location from a different document type/origin (a company tariff filed with FERC vs. a 2007 trade-press story). Williams' current facilities page adds a third data point, listing the pipeline specifically at 'Hood County, Texas'. Only State/Country level is filled on the sheet (StartLocation/EndLocation/Prefecture-District cells are blank) -- I did not add city/county-level values since the sources describe a tri-county corridor (Jack/Parker/Hood) rather than two crisp point endpoints, and forcing a single start/end pair would be a judgment call beyond what's cleanly sourced; leaving StartLocation/EndLocation blank and only sourcing the existing Texas/US values that are already on the sheet.

summary: P4416 Worsham-Steed Pipeline: confirmed (caveat), no existence/duplicate/classification concerns -- Status/Fuel/Location corroborated by 2+ independent sources (tier=high), StartYear1/Length/Diameter rest on one strong contemporaneous NGI account (tier=medium, no UNRESOLVED).
